items.summary: Unrefereed candidate. A proof that for every n >= 1 and real c, every non-real eigenvalue of the 2n x 2n indefinite tridiagonal pencil H_c - lambda S (diagonal c, off-diagonal 1, S = diag(1,...,1,-1,...,-1)) satisfies |lambda - c| < 2 and |lambda + c| < 2. This is Conjecture 5.3 of Davies and Levitin (Linear Algebra Appl. 448, 2014), and it implies the closed-disk form of AIM 2015 Problem 11.1. It was previously known for n <= 3 and for eigenvalues equidistant from c and -c (Öztürk 2023). A standard Weyl-function mechanism, applied to the known Chebyshev form of the characteristic equation, reduces the conjecture to a comparison lemma for an explicit Lorentzian sum over the zeros of U_{n-1}; the comparison lemma and its proof are the original contribution. It is proved by explicit estimates with finitely many Arb-certified constants for n >= 8, elementary arguments for n <= 2, and, for 3 <= n <= 7, an explicit estimate plus a short interval certificate with rational endpoints and Arb ball arithmetic. Certified examples show that the lens fails for some other spectral measures, for a balanced pencil with one weakened coupling, and for unbalanced pencils. The package contains the manuscript, certificates, regression tests, semantic negative controls and review records. Provenance: the research, proof and text were produced by an AI research agent (Claude, Anthropic) under the direction of the publisher, Evidence Press; no human mathematical contribution is claimed, and no human specialist has checked the proof. Internal replay and model-based reviews only; no formal verification, independent reproduction, specialist or journal peer review; novelty is established only within a bounded literature search.
items.title: A proof of the Davies–Levitin lens conjecture for the indefinite tridiagonal pencil

items.summary: The rapid progression of large language models is extending AI from passive content generation into the active workflows of engineering and scientific discovery. This shift raises a compelling question: can AI be both the object of development and an active participant in building next-generation AI systems? We explore this question by building Qwen-Planner-Agent within a closed-loop AI-for-AI framework for scalable development and iterative improvement. Mobile planning offers a demanding test of this approach: complex, long-horizon tasks challenge agent reliability, while costly real-device interaction limits development scalability. The framework connects data production, model training, and deployment through a shared action-feedback-verification contract. (i) AI for Data builds a human-gated agentic data flywheel in which specialized agents construct tasks, collect interaction trajectories, curate and balance training data, and use training feedback to guide subsequent data generation. (ii) AI for Training combines a supervised planning cold start with hybrid-environment online agentic reinforcement learning, where we introduce Competence-Aware Reward-and-Advantage Engineering (CARE) to reduce reasoning and tool-use costs while preserving task performance. (iii) AI drives model--harness co-evolution through an execution-evidence-driven loop that orchestrates memory, skills, and tools at runtime and feeds structured action feedback and preserved failure traces back into coordinated model and harness adaptation. Qwen-Planner-Agent achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated models and systems on MobilePA-Bench, improving over its base model across tool use, memory, skills, and sub-agent coordination. Further evaluations of our model show improvements across non-mobile agentic benchmarks while largely preserving general capabilities.
items.title: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents

items.summary: Global-to-local load transfer remains a critical – yet largely unstandardized – step in the structural assessment of floating structures. This paper presents the results of package WP2.2 from the OC7 project Phase II, which establishes a cross-industry benchmark for the workflows connecting global performance analysis (based on integrated loads analysis, ILA) and the local structural assessment (based on finite-element analysis, FEA). The study evaluates a spectrum of industry practices, including sequential approaches with the FEA following the ILA, fully integrated time-domain approaches with hydro-structural coupling, and simplified ILA-only approaches. Using the VolturnUS-S reference semi-submersible, the models were first harmonized through mass and inertia, static, and modal verifications. Structural responses were then compared across three primary scenarios: topside-only excitation, irregular waves, and combined wind and wave loading. The results establish a structured comparison framework, highlighting how specific modelling choices and load transfer techniques directly influence confidence in design processes. The findings offer practical guidance to reduce uncertainty in “global-to-local” design workflows.
items.title: OC7 Project Phase II: Comparison of Global-to-Local Load Transfer Approaches in Floating Structures

items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
items.title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22967519 . This paper looks at what happens when we trust an AI coding agent's work without independently checking what actually changed. The authors show a case where a protected file was changed, but GTB still returned VERIFIED because the file was left out of the verification process. I thought one of the strongest parts of the paper was the distinction between stopping an agent from doing something and actually being able to prove that it didn't do it . The paper also does a good job of showing the attack in practice, explaining why the verification failed, and suggesting ways to make the process more reliable. Major issues The experiment focuses on GTB, so testing other coding-agent or verification systems would help show whether the issue is specific to GTB or appears more broadly. The proposed fixes have not yet been independently tested. Testing them against the same attack, along with a few variations, would make the results more convincing. Minor issues Including the exact software versions and experimental environment would make the experiment easier to reproduce. A simple diagram showing the normal verification path and where the modified file gets excluded would make the main failure easier to understand. It would also be useful to state how many times the attack was repeated and whether the same result occurred consistently Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they did not use generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.
items.title: PREreview of "Beyond Agent Self-Reporting: Evidence-Based Verification of Autonomous AI Software Work"

items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. Keywords: LLM agents; continuity; branching; fork; recovery; relational identity; longitudinal interaction; agent memory; persona; harness; path dependence; provenance
items.title: FORK, RECOVERY, AND HISTORICALLY ORGANIZED CONTINUITY IN A LONGITUDINAL LLM–HUMAN INTERACTION: A Naturalistic Case Study

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.
items.title: STEMBench: an Inspect-AI benchmark harness for research-grade STEM agent tasks

items.summary: This corrected data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “Human protein complex interfaces reveal candidate assembly roles for initiator methionine excision.” It asks which human protein N-terminal positions engage assembly partners and whether their interface environments nominate specific roles for methionine removal. The archive combines a human structural census with terminal-boundary sensitivity analyses, evidence-qualified comparisons and partner-resolved proteasome geometry. Its central biological message is that the possible importance of methionine removal depends not only on sequence, but also on which partner an N-terminal position encounters in a particular assembly context. Sequence-class associations and an evidence-qualified atlas identify candidates for direct tests of verified terminal processing, partner engagement, complex assembly and function. The census comprises 7,246 human biological assemblies, 22,291 chain-level observations and 1,191 proteins. The primary sequence-class analysis includes 1,123 analyzable proteins. At the descriptive threshold of at least 25% burial, interface engagement occurs in 37.5% of MetAP-permissive and 47.5% of nonpermissive residue-2 sequence classes; the assembly-chain-count-adjusted odds ratio is 0.65 (p = 7.6 × 10⁻⁴). First-observed coordinate-boundary filtering retains 845 proteins, including 175 interface-engaged permissive-class candidates. These are distinct analysis populations and should not be interchanged with the original 261-protein permissive-class candidate set. The corrected analyses distinguish annotation-selected sequence positions, observed coordinate boundaries, modeled residue identities and independent proteoform evidence. Partner-resolved comparisons cover 22 selected PSMA4, PSMA6 and PSMA7 chain observations across seven PDB entries. They distinguish PSMA7 partner environments, a PSMA6 chaperone-facing backbone and PSMA4 multi-partner packing. Reconstructed group-level tests use explicit membership definitions, eligible backgrounds, boundary sensitivities and multiplicity corrections. A histone-symbol association is supported within the tested structural collection, including peptide-recognition contexts; proteasome enrichment is sensitive to boundary eligibility and multiplicity treatment and is not presented as a robust, universal association. The release provides the corrected supplementary datasets, analysis code, frozen inputs, partner-contact tables, figure source data and artwork, reconstruction outputs, and documentation needed to distinguish current results from labeled historical provenance. The Supplementary Information, main figure legends and five main and three supplementary figures are synchronized with the approved scientific materials of 25 September 2026. The current plotting component contains the exact source inputs and reproduces the approved figure presentation; earlier renderings remain labeled provenance. The original census measurements are retained where appropriate, while corrected labels, sensitivity analyses and revised interpretations are explicitly documented. The synchronization does not add new structural calculations, statistical findings or experimental measurements and is not a census-wide reanalysis. Structural observations are not independent biological replicates, and deposited contexts do not establish an ordered maturation trajectory. Modeled Met1 does not demonstrate physiological methionine retention; first-observed Ser2 does not establish sample-specific excision, acetylation or a free terminal amino group. Incomplete modeled atoms are flagged rather than rebuilt. Pair-only burial values are nonadditive. The archive supports hypothesis generation and reproducible structural analysis, not demonstrated processing causality, disease mechanisms or clinical prediction. items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. Keywords: LLM agents; continuity; branching; fork; recovery; relational identity; longitudinal interaction; agent memory; persona; harness; path dependence; provenance

items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.

Abstract: Under the communist regime, the evidence related to education in Hungarian mother tongue was under restricted access, except for two statistical yearbooks in which only limited data was available. At present, 28 years after the fall of the Romanian communist regime, public access to archived records is considerably easier. However, for the period 1948-1989, a statistical report on education in the Hungarian language hasn't been done so far. Given the lack of descriptive data, our inquiry has sought to portray a history of Hungarian mother tongue school education in Romania in the communist era as it has been revealed following our enterprise of collecting, selecting, sorting and analyzing data from relevant statistical yearbooks, statistical reports on education and the other published or unpublished statistical records. After the reconstruction of a satisfactory set of documents containing data on the number of schools, number of enrolled pupils and number of teaching staff, our research was focused on a trend analysis. Finally, contrasting these findings with the legislative and political context, we tried to provide some answers on how and why the communist regime had limited the mother tongue education opportunities of the Hungarian population in Romania. items.summary: This corrected data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “Human protein complex interfaces reveal candidate assembly roles for initiator methionine excision.” It asks which human protein N-terminal positions engage assembly partners and whether their interface environments nominate specific roles for methionine removal. The archive combines a human structural census with terminal-boundary sensitivity analyses, evidence-qualified comparisons and partner-resolved proteasome geometry. Its central biological message is that the possible importance of methionine removal depends not only on sequence, but also on which partner an N-terminal position encounters in a particular assembly context. Sequence-class associations and an evidence-qualified atlas identify candidates for direct tests of verified terminal processing, partner engagement, complex assembly and function. The census comprises 7,246 human biological assemblies, 22,291 chain-level observations and 1,191 proteins. The primary sequence-class analysis includes 1,123 analyzable proteins. At the descriptive threshold of at least 25% burial, interface engagement occurs in 37.5% of MetAP-permissive and 47.5% of nonpermissive residue-2 sequence classes; the assembly-chain-count-adjusted odds ratio is 0.65 (p = 7.6 × 10⁻⁴). First-observed coordinate-boundary filtering retains 845 proteins, including 175 interface-engaged permissive-class candidates. These are distinct analysis populations and should not be interchanged with the original 261-protein permissive-class candidate set. The corrected analyses distinguish annotation-selected sequence positions, observed coordinate boundaries, modeled residue identities and independent proteoform evidence. Partner-resolved comparisons cover 22 selected PSMA4, PSMA6 and PSMA7 chain observations across seven PDB entries. They distinguish PSMA7 partner environments, a PSMA6 chaperone-facing backbone and PSMA4 multi-partner packing. Reconstructed group-level tests use explicit membership definitions, eligible backgrounds, boundary sensitivities and multiplicity corrections. A histone-symbol association is supported within the tested structural collection, including peptide-recognition contexts; proteasome enrichment is sensitive to boundary eligibility and multiplicity treatment and is not presented as a robust, universal association. Reads the arrays under  benchmark2/ and produces every Benchmark II figure and table in the paper. Both notebooks are also present in the code repository with cleared outputs so they are diff-friendly under version control. The copies in this deposit are the same notebooks executed once against the data files included here, with the resulting figures and tables embedded as outputs. How to use For viewing only: open the notebooks under notebooks_executed/ in any Jupyter viewer (including GitHub's renderer and nbviewer ). All figures are embedded. No installation required. For re-execution from data: clone the evaluating-generative-models code repository, follow its installation instructions in README.md , place the contents of this deposit's benchmark2/ directory under data/benchmark2/ (documented in notebooks/README.md ), and run the cleared notebooks under notebooks/ . Outputs should match the executed notebooks included here. For full regeneration from checkpoints: requires the dileptonic ttbar neutrino regression dataset (Raine et al., 2023) and trained model checkpoints produced by scripts/train.py . See the code repository's README.md for the full pipeline. Contents: the IntentValidator pipeline source snapshot and run configurations; the per-claim datasets of the canonical agent run, of the all-repository human comparison cohort (with its protocol, draw listings and order of events) and of the superseded first human cohort, plus the re-runs that document the effect of the pipeline's timeouts; the 186-pattern NFR claim catalog, boilerplate-stripping rules and the full match table; the extraction-validity ladder and regression scripts; the manual-validation kit (stratified samples, rubric, blind labelling tool, both human raters' sheets with untouched exports and SHA-256 sums, three disclosed LLM annotation passes with per-item rationales and provenance, the LLM-judge sensitivity, the adjudication queue, a recall probe of unflagged pull requests with blind sheets and a disclosed LLM screen, and a kit for a rater from outside the author team); the consistency analysis on the human-validated claims, the Maintainability-Index floor sensitivity and the all-language cross-check of the index against independent Halstead implementations (per-claim results); every analysis script that regenerates the manuscript's numbers and figures; and a checksum manifest of every file with named reproduction checks. The archive carries the replication tree only; the manuscript itself is not included. The AIDev dataset itself is not redistributed; obtain it from its own Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.16919272). The 25 September 2026 audit revision adds explicit sampling and interpretation limitations, corrected stratification of diagnostic agreement intervals, clarified nominal instrument coverage, and reproducibility notes. Original human labels and canonical claim verdicts are preserved; catalogue label/rubric conflicts remain for human reassessment. See replication/09-paper/emse-2026/replication/REVIEW-NOTES-2026-09-25.md.

items.summary: This record provides reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI”. The study evaluates scientific-AI fidelity by distinguishing assigned scientific objects, realized scientific objects, lineage or pathway fidelity, terminal scientific fidelity and claim boundaries.   The archive contains detailed evidence registries, comparison specifications, provenance and audit records, structured source records, manuscript source materials, display assets, and code for assembling and rendering the supplied publication materials. It also preserves the available historical CoralTemp/Coral Reef Watch daily-classification source excerpt used in the documented evidence chain.   The released materials support inspection of the reported evidence, scientific-object assignments, realized-use verification, lineage-resolved comparisons and presentation-level reproduction. They do not constitute a complete executable end-to-end reproduction of all scientific analyses. Complete raw-input and terminal-reference payloads, full benchmark execution and scoring pipelines, original scientific figure-generation programs and the original pinned scientific execution environments are not included. Public upstream scientific products and their provenance are documented in the manuscript and archive.   The archive should therefore be interpreted as a provenance-rich reproducibility and audit package rather than as a general benchmark of scientific-AI accuracy or reliability.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for "Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI"

items.summary: This record contains the public reproducibility package supporting the study “Persistent spatial organization and period-dependent associations in Beijing’s surface thermal–moisture environment”. The package includes the model-ready analytical dataset, temporal-screening and provenance records, cross-validation folds, model parameters and random-seed records, formal scripts for pooled and period-specific XGBoost–SHAP analyses, GeoDetector analysis, stored model outputs, quality-control and checksum records, and selected figure-source materials. The study comprises seven quality-controlled summer observation periods: 2000, 2004, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2016, and 2019. The primary reproducibility target of this package is the reported statistical analysis beginning from the archived ModelReady dataset. Production scripts preserve the original execution paths used during the formal analysis; users reproducing the analyses should update input and output paths to their local repository location. Upstream geospatial preprocessing scripts are retained for methodological provenance and may require the original third-party source products and local GIS configuration. Original Landsat, GLC_FCS30D, WorldPop, and Copernicus DEM source archives are not redistributed in this record and should be obtained from their respective providers. Detailed package structure, provenance, execution scope, and reproducibility notes are provided in the included README. Licensing: Data, documentation, and other original research materials created by the authors are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license. Source code created by the authors is released under the MIT License. Third-party and derived source materials remain subject to the terms of their original providers and are not relicensed by this record.

items.summary: A benchmark harness for evaluating LLM agents on research-grade STEM tasks, built on Inspect AI. Each task is a self-contained contract folder that the harness loads, stages into a sandbox, runs through an agent, and scores without task-specific harness code. WHAT THIS ARCHIVE CONTAINS Harness source code: task loading, Inspect task/solver construction, tool surface (bash, python, data exploration, literature search, document reading, submission validation), Docker and local sandbox backends, scorers, and the CLI entry points for running, grading, and aggregating. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. Evaluation run logs (.eval files) are not published. The reported scores are in LEADERBOARD.md, the per-task CSVs under leaderboards/, and report.html, which embeds the per-run agent trajectories. One task's payload (ABIDE-derived) is never redistributed: its source data is CC-BY-NC-SA and derives from human neuroimaging data. A preparation script rebuilds it locally from the source archive and verifies the result against the published checksums. Published reference papers are not redistributed. Every external reference is cited by DOI with title, authors, venue, and a resolvable link. REPRODUCIBILITY REPRODUCING.md is the step-by-step checklist. Two limits are stated up front: reported scores come from hosted preview model snapshots run without a fixed seed or temperature, so they are samples from a distribution rather than bit-reproducible values; and dependency versions are not pinned in this version of the archive. DATA_LICENSES.md records the provenance and licence of every task's data, including the attribution notices required by the CC-BY-4.0 sources. LICENCE Code, task contracts, graders, reference solutions, and documentation are MIT. Task descriptions and the synthetic data payloads are CC-BY-4.0 and are covered by the companion dataset record.
items.title: STEMBench: an Inspect-AI benchmark harness for research-grade STEM agent tasks
